claims.text: OCR-2.0 theory (all artificial optical signals as 'characters') + 580M unified end-to-end model: 80M high-compression encoder (1024px to 256 tokens) + long-context decoder; plain/formatted outputs (markdown/tikz/smiles/kern); region-guided interactive OCR; dynamic resolution; multi-page OCR.
claims.context: Full-paper abstract/architecture/conclusion; token-economics figures consumed (X03 exhibit).

claims.text: Paper's positioning: structurally simpler than OCR-1.0 pipelines, more OCR-focused than LVLMs with superior reported performance — vendor-style superiority framing quarantined to own OCR-2.0 suites.

Training is predominantly synthetic data-engine centered (PaddleOCR pseudo ground truth, six rendering tools for formulas/tables/music/geometry/charts, Nougat-method plus Chinese markdown pairs) with Common-Crawl PDF extraction alongside — rendered/pseudo-centered, not exclusively synthetic.

limitations.text: Own-suite evaluation; same-protocol generalist head-to-head not found (gap G03 preserved).
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.finding: Full body consumed: OCR-2.0 theory, encoder/decoder design, interactivity and multi-page features verified.
No cross-model numeric ranking constructed; qualitative contract preserved.
